scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The output stops halfway
scenes.caption: Asha runs a synthetic batch with three valid alerts. The first output commits, then the prepared output fault stops the second. A reliable workflow must identify what succeeded and what remains pending.
scenes.dialogue: Partial success is different from complete success.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Do not erase the checkpoint
scenes.caption: Deleting the output history before retrying can repeat the first output. Ignoring the stop can lose the remaining records. Preserve the input batch, committed IDs and pending work while the authorised operator resolves the fault.
scenes.dialogue: A safe retry starts from preserved evidence.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Choose the failure response
scenes.caption: Empty input should produce an explicit no-change result. Malformed data goes to quarantine. An unavailable output stops the batch with a checkpoint; retry only after the underlying fault is resolved. A changed payload under an existing ID needs review, not overwrite.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Choose the retry plan
scenes.caption: Should Asha delete the ledger and start again, pretend the whole batch succeeded, or retry the preserved batch after the fault is resolved while skipping already committed identical events?
scenes.dialogue: Keep pending work and completed work distinct.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A visible recovery trace
scenes.caption: The model keeps A01 committed and marks A02 and A03 pending. On retry, it skips the identical A01 event and commits the remaining two. All three unique outputs are present, and no real notification was ever sent.
scenes.dialogue: The action log explains what the retry changed.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the failure lab
scenes.caption: Classify the fault pack, run the partial-failure simulation and inspect the retry. Then respond to an existing ID arriving with different content. The model demonstrates retry safety without promising real-world exactly-once delivery.
